name: Kasm Workspaces

modes.label: Self-hosted Workspaces licence (Starter: $10/user or $20/concurrent session)

sizes.name: Starter licence (compute on your own servers)

modes.commit_note: Annual licence subscription billed upfront; $120/named user/yr or $240/concurrent session/yr; checkout caps at 25 seats.
modes.note: Starter licence = $10 per named user per month or $20 per concurrent session per month, sold only as an annual subscription billed upfront ($120/user/yr or $240/session/yr), 1-25 seats via online checkout (Starter version only; >25 = Enterprise quote). Self-supported (no support); support add-on 20% (Standard) / 40% (Premium) of licence cost; PureVPN egress add-on $8/seat/month. Compute is your own servers/cloud on top. hour stays null because the licence is per seat, not per hour.

modes.label: Kasm-managed Workspaces as a Service (minimum 25 users)
modes.note: Added 2026-09-28 (missing-providers audit). https://kasm.com/cloud-vs-server: "Cloud Kasm-Managed - Minimum of 25 users", Workspaces as a Service; Kasm Hosted SaaS is an Enterprise feature (https://kasm.com/community-edition), price by quote.

modes.label: Kasm Cloud Personal (hosted disposable browser/desktop, flat monthly with hour cap)
modes.note: Self-serve monthly subscription, no annual option shown. Hours are hard monthly caps: Browser 100 h (20-min idle timeout), Desktop 200 h (30-min idle timeout), OSINT 300 h (60-min idle timeout); no overage price published. vCPU is a minimum with burst allowed; RAM is a hard limit. Sessions are deleted after use, no software installs, no root, no persistence (link Dropbox/OneDrive/Google Drive instead). Concurrent sessions per account not published (max_vms null). Purchases non-refundable; cancel at end of term (Cloud SaaS terms). Alt: consumer isolation product, not a programmable sandbox.

plans.name: Starter (self-host)
plans.note: $10/named user/month or $20/concurrent session/month, billed annually upfront; 1-25 seats; self-supported only (no support tickets); support add-on 20%/40% of licence; PureVPN egress $8/seat/month optional; compute not included.

plans.name: Enterprise / Kasm hosted
plans.note: Request a quote; Kasm-managed cloud: minimum 25 users, per-user annual cloud subscription, single-tenant; HA only for 100+ users. (Cloud Personal FAQ says SaaS instances for 'businesses with 50 or more uses' - older doc, conflicts with 25.)

plans.name: Community Edition (self-host)
plans.note: Free, non-commercial only (individuals, non-profits, testing); 5 concurrent sessions; community support; compute is your own.

perf_source: No benchmark row: provider is not in ComputeSDK results or the HPC run (as of 2026-09-28). See research/perf-map.json.
caveats: Starter self-host licence is $10/named user/month or $20/concurrent session/month on an annual prepaid subscription (1-25 seats) plus your own compute; hosted business SaaS is quote-only (min 25 users, annual). The only self-serve Kasm-hosted compute is Cloud Personal ($10/$20/$40 per month with 100/200/300 h caps).
Self-hosted: compute is your own servers or cloud VMs, on top of the licence.
Community Edition is free for individuals/non-profits (5 concurrent sessions), non-commercial.
Streams containerised Linux desktops/browsers (KasmVNC); Windows via RDP servers.

Kasm also sells Workspaces for Oracle Click-to-Subscribe (ephemeral workspaces on OCI, no persistence): Developer $40, Business $60, AI (GPU) $250 per user/month with 200/200/240 h monthly caps and 30/30/60-min idle timeouts. Machine sizes are not published, so it is not priced.

snapshot_auto.quote: Stop - The session is stopped, preserving the disk state.
snapshot_auto.note: No automatic snapshot. keepalive_expiration_action (group setting; default timeout 1 h) can delete, stop (container disk kept = persistent disk, processes lost) or pause (docker pause: 'preserving the disk,  process and memory state' but it stays in RAM/swap, not checkpointed). Persistent profiles (host/NFS volume or S3 via kasm-profile-sync) restore only the user's home directory on each launch.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: Administrators can create new docker images from active container-based Workspace sessions.
snapshot_on_demand.note: 'Create Image from Session' in the admin Sessions page = docker commit of the running container (disk only, no memory), optional push to a registry; a new Workspace entry is created so new sessions boot from it (template-style fork). Admin console only; not in the public Developer API endpoint list. Container workspaces only.

harness_api.note: Public Developer API covers request_kasm/destroy_kasm/exec_command_kasm (generic exec), screenshots, users, egress, casting, staging; no agent-harness endpoints. 1.17 only adds a 'Kasm AI registry' spotlight entry (images). Latest docs are 1.17.0.

egress_allowlist.quote: If checked, all requests will be denied unless the domain is added to the Domain Whitelist, or the category of the domain is set to allow.
egress_allowlist.note: Web Filter Policies (domain allow/deny lists, deny-by-default, URL categories, per group/workspace) exist, but they are enforced by a Kasm Squid proxy installed inside the workspace image and wired via http_proxy=127.0.0.1:3128 (workspaces-core-images install_squid.sh), i.e. inside the container, not outside it. Other network controls: Egress Providers/Gateways tunnel all session traffic through OpenVPN/WireGuard (routing, with kill-switch iptables in the container netns, not an allowlist); admins can pin workspaces to custom Docker networks on self-managed agents (host firewall is the operator's own).

ingress_rules.quote: Any authenticated user may join a shared session if the URL is known.
ingress_rules.note: Sessions are only reachable as streamed desktops through the authenticated Kasm web/proxy tier; sharing is opt-in (allow_kasm_sharing group setting), view-only by default; Casting URLs can be unauthenticated but protected by ReCAPTCHA, referrer and per-IP rate limits. No feature for publishing arbitrary app ports; no per-session IP allowlist documented.

secret_proxy.note: No credential-injecting proxy documented. Secrets reach sessions as env vars (Docker Run Config / exec_command_kasm environment) or mounted storage; Egress Credentials are VPN credentials; S3 persistent profiles use presigned URLs so the container never holds the S3 key (profile sync only).

volume_attach.quote: Storage Mappings allow administrators to create and attach custom and ephemeral docker volumes in Kasm Workspace Containers.
volume_attach.note: Also Volume Mappings (host/NFS paths bound into every session of a workspace) and user cloud-storage mappings (Google Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive, Nextcloud, S3, rclone).

volume_shared.quote: This effectively will act as a file share.
volume_shared.note: A host directory (NFS/SMB/etc. in multi-server deployments) mapped into all concurrent sessions of the workspace, mode rw or ro per mapping; {username}/{user_id}/{image_id} tokens give per-user paths.
